sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the web framework tools, database session, study data types and date tools, then creates the router for study routes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the main app needs one router object for these routes.

sections.name: StudyCreate
sections.title: New study request fields
sections.what: Describes what a new study needs: name, description, study type, optional survey link, target audience data, sample size, markets and languages. Markets default to US and languages to EN.
sections.why: Likely reason: the defaults cover the most common case.
sections.watch_out: Target audience is free-form data. Other code may depend on its keys, which this file does not check.

sections.name: StudyResponse
sections.title: Study summary returned
sections.what: Defines the summary fields returned for a study: ID, name, type, status, target size, response counts and creation time.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps responses to a fixed set of fields.

sections.name: create_study
sections.title: Create a new study
sections.what: Saves a new study in planning status with a generated ID and returns its summary with a 201 created status.
sections.why: Likely reason: new studies start in planning so nothing goes live before it is set up.
sections.watch_out: The creator is fixed to system with a TODO.

sections.name: get_study
sections.title: Fetch one study
sections.what: Returns the summary for a study ID, or a not found error.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: launch_study
sections.title: Start a study running
sections.what: Starts a study only when it is ready. Marks it running, records the launch time and returns a run ID.
sections.why: Likely reason: a study should not go live before it is ready.
sections.watch_out: The run ID is the study ID itself, so there is no separate run record. The code does not say why.

sections.name: get_study_report
sections.title: Study progress report (partial)
sections.what: Returns the study name, status and a progress percentage of responses collected against the target. The analytics sections are empty.
sections.why: The TODO notes show the full report is not built yet.
sections.watch_out: The percentage is only computed when the target is above zero, and the rest of the report is empty.

summary: Defines the web addresses for creating, reading, launching and reporting on research studies.
purpose: Lets a user set up a study, start it once it is ready, and check its progress.
why: Likely reason: a study moves through set stages, and these routes control those stages.
how: Defines request and response shapes. Creating saves a new planning-stage study. Launching checks for ready status, then marks it running and records the time. The report route reads the stored counts.
inputs: Study name, description, study type, optional survey link, target audience data, sample size, markets, languages, and a study ID.
outputs: Study summaries, a launch message with a run ID, a progress report, and not found or bad-status errors.
risks: Launching is refused unless the study is ready, but nothing in this file sets a study to ready. The report is partial. The creator is fixed to system. Target audience data is not checked.
debug: If launch fails, check the study status first. If a report shows zero progress, check that the completed count is being updated elsewhere. Check that the study ID is correct.
